requirements.applicability: always

requirements.summary: Seven operations; ACTIVATE at genesis only; payload changes only on ACTIVATE, EDIT, TRANSFER; owner changes only on TRANSFER; event_data empty on ACTIVATE and EDIT.

requirements.summary: User signature over fields 1 to 12 under [1, 'dpp token v1'] with actor_keyID and counterparty anyone; server signature over fields 1 to 13 with passport_id; both via BRC-100 createSignature.

requirements.summary: The seven chain invariants, including the three-way spend check.
requirements.applicability: always

requirements.summary: The owner-tier blob's SHA-256 is field 11; a blob against an empty commitment is a refusal; disclosure is cryptographic.
requirements.applicability: always

requirements.summary: Every restricted field of every tier forms one object encrypted to the owner under one commitment; a legitimate or authority reader receives a disclosure, the fields of its tiers and no others, re-encrypted under the same protocol and key identifier with the reader's identity key as counterparty; a disclosure is not committed on chain and never carries a field of a tier the reader is not entitled to.
requirements.applicability: when a profile declares a tier beyond owner
requirements.notes: The offline reference example checks the one owner ciphertext against field 11, opens it, validates the complete object and re-encrypts the permitted subset for the already entitled reader. SDK wallet tests decrypt to two distinct audiences and check the original commitment, wrong-recipient refusal and mismatched commitment. Entitlement verification and delivery are deployment responsibilities.

requirements.summary: Verified means signatures, linkage and inclusion; inclusion has three outcomes and an unreachable header source is pending, never failed; a proof that does not contain the transaction fails.

requirements.summary: The seventeen fields: the version 1 rules for the shared fields, event_data JSON or empty at most 4096 bytes on every operation, payload_public at most 65535 bytes, lineage_genesis and previous_outpoint empty or 36 bytes, control_linkage and authorisation_commitment empty or 32 bytes, control_linkage empty on ISSUE.
requirements.applicability: always

requirements.summary: Four operations: ISSUE at genesis only; controller_key changes only on TRANSFER; payload_public and payload_owner_hash unchanged on RETIRE; RETIRE terminal; event_data JSON or empty on every operation; the version 1 vocabulary is a profile's property of event_data.
requirements.applicability: always

requirements.summary: Both preimages are VarInt-framed and opened by a domain tag (dpp-record-v2/actor-signature, dpp-record-v2/publisher-signature); keys derive under [1, 'dpp token v2'] with actor_keyID and passport_id as key identifiers, counterparty anyone; a version 1 signature verifies under nothing in version 2 and a signature in the wrong slot fails.
requirements.applicability: always

requirements.summary: The nine invariants: one DPP output; the genesis rules and a genesis that spends an admitted output refused; no ISSUE, no state after RETIRE and only an UPDATE after a version 1 state; previous_outpoint equal to the spent tip on txid, index and structural spend; lineage_genesis equal to the chain genesis and never assumed; immutable passport_id; controller_key only on TRANSFER and unchanged on the upgrade; RETIRE payload immutable; control proven; no downgrade.
requirements.applicability: always

requirements.summary: On every UPDATE, TRANSFER and RETIRE the actor proves control of the previous state in the fixed order equality, named authority, linkage; the linkage scalar is the BRC-69 specific key linkage of the controller key derivation, read big-endian modulo the curve order, 32 bytes in field 14 and 64 lower-case hexadecimal characters wherever it is text; a scalar beside a settled proof is refused as redundant; a missing or non-linking scalar is refused; authorities are the verifier's policy, empty unless it names keys, and never the record's.
requirements.applicability: always

requirements.summary: authorisation_commitment is the SHA-256 of a profile-defined authorisation record; the record model accepts it on any operation, a profile says where it is required, and a verifier that cannot obtain the record reports the artefact unavailable and not the state invalid.
requirements.applicability: always

requirements.summary: Verified means signatures, linkage and inclusion under each state's own version, with the upgrade rule at the boundary and the optional publisher check; a mixed history is verified state by state.
requirements.applicability: always

requirements.notes: Kept on 12 November 2026 when spec/gs1-discovery.md was cut to the DPP identifier rules; the rule stood in its section 1 before and no row assessed it. Limits: a linkset request is answered with JSON whatever the Accept, with no page of links for a person; the general GS1 Digital Link compression is not decoded, as the profile declares; TLS is the deployment's; the tests run over plain HTTP on one machine with the test wallet and an index in the process; GS1's own resolver test suite was not run against a generated application; the published starter 0.1.0-beta.1 does not resolve; and the hosted reference application's resolver is still not evidence this repository can show. requirements.summary: A profile held by a binding travels as a profile bundle inside a dpp-evidence-package@1: the binding file in its exact bytes, every artefact it lists, the notices it lists and a descriptor, each an inventory entry in the schemas category, with no member added to the manifest. A destination registers a carried binding only under the registration rules: trust comes from its own list of binding digests and never from the descriptor, the manifest or the exporter's signature; a binding other than the one it holds or expects is refused as a substitution; every artefact is held to the length and SHA-256 the binding records; each cause has its own refusal; and a refused or incomplete profile leaves a payload unknown, never pass. The descriptor states in fixed words that validation under a carried profile says nothing about payload_owner_hash.

requirements.summary: An update check compares the active version of a profile held by a binding with the candidate set of files the next version would list, and answers with a change report and a proposed binding. It registers nothing and leaves the active binding, its artefacts and what a registry answers for them unchanged. The report lists every artefact of either version as added, removed, changed or unchanged, with role, licence, byte length and SHA-256 on each side; for a JSON-LD context, every term added, removed or redefined, a removed or redefined term marked as breaking, as is a context that no longer names another the active version lists, and a context that could not be read reported as not compared, never as unchanged; every other artefact by length and digest only, saying so. A candidate that is the active files byte for byte reports no change and proposes nothing; otherwise the proposal keeps the id at a higher version with a binding digest of its own, or nothing is proposed and the reasons are given. A proposal registers only under the registration rules: its digest on the registry's trusted list, which the report never adds to, and never over the (id, version) it was derived from. The report states what the check did not do, the acceptance vectors among it, and the same input gives the same report and the same bytes, whatever order the candidate lists its files in.
requirements.applicability: when a profile held by a binding is checked against files its source publishes again
requirements.notes: Added 2026-11-16 with the rule. The tests run the check on a binding written for the test and on the bundled eu-battery@1: after a check the active version resolves to the same object and the same bytes and nothing else is registered; a changed context lists the terms it removes, redefines and adds; the bundled core context without its import of the assessment context is breaking although none of its own terms changed, and a context that names another listed context now is listed for review; a changed shapes file is compared by length and digest and the report says so; a candidate of the active files reports no change and proposes nothing, in any order; the same files in another order, two new ones included, give the same report and the same proposed bytes; a proposal is refused as binding-untrusted until its digest is on the trusted list, its files are held to its own record, and a proposal written back under the active id and version is refused as binding-conflict even with that digest trusted. The check runs no acceptance vector, because the package carries no validation engine: examples/check-binding-update.mjs, which CI runs, runs the example profile's vectors under both versions in a review registry and shows the two that passed now failing for the term the report marked as breaking. A changed or new licence is listed for review, not decided. No application or index runs a check: it is a maintenance step, and nothing activates a proposal.

requirements.clause: §2, a package that carries more than one passport
requirements.summary: A package may carry the evidence of more than one passport, as a complete export of an application does, under one manifest with no member added. Its passportId names the export as urn:bsv:dpp:evidence-export:sha256 over the canonical list of the passport identifiers carried, so a signature made for one selection verifies for no other; each passport's own evidence sits in a folder of its own as the package its exporter signed, with that manifest listed as a reports entry and each of its files in the category its own manifest gives it; the outer signature does not stand in for the inner one; a reader that expects one passport refuses an export by its passportId and a reader of exports refuses a package whose name is not the one its carried passports give; and an export that carries restricted records declares all-tiers and that it is a recovery backup, while one under the public disclosure carries none of them.
requirements.applicability: when an application exports more than one passport's evidence in one package, or restores such a package
requirements.notes: Added 2026-11-15 with the paragraph. The one implementation is the application starter, whose tests run in the generated application and not in this workspace: packages/create-dpp-app/scripts/scaffold-check.mjs scaffolds it against the packed candidates and runs them. Its export signs the manifest through the platform wallet under the evidence package protocol with the export's name as key identifier, and the package inspects on structure, inventory and signature with the protocol package's own inspection. It carries, for each passport, the index's bounded package or the parts of its complete export exactly as the index signed them, the application's journal with each sealed owner tier, each acceptance record as an authority entry, the brands, offers and claims that belong to the passports, a profile bundle and an EPCIS recovery snapshot; the public form carries the index's evidence, the readings, the profile files and the public form of the source scopes its operator names, and a test searches every byte of it for restricted product values, the sealed owner tiers, the source credential, the index tokens, the deployment's secrets, cursor material and the source's address. Both forms are searched for every configured secret before they are written, and an export that would carry one is refused. The restore verifies the whole package before it writes: the exporter's signature under a key the operator gives, every file against the inventory both ways, each journal as a lineage, the index's signature on its own evidence, the bundle against the destination's trusted binding digests and the digests the carried states declare, and the snapshot by the module's checks. It refuses by name a package under another exporter key, a missing file or record, an altered or unlisted file, a manifest signed for another selection, a substituted binding with and without its digest trusted, a package about one passport and the public form; a destination record that differs stops it with nothing written, and a second restore writes nothing. The exit exercise restores into a deployment with another storage adapter and the bundle as its profile resolver, with the first deployment's database and index stopped and every other host out of reach, and both passports then read there check for check and finding for finding as they did, and an UPDATE written there verifies. Limits: both deployments run in one test process; each index is the reference index's code over in-memory storage with its header checks off, so no reading is a statement about inclusion in a block; the wallet is the test wallet, and the second deployment holding the same keys stands in for the wallet's own recovery, since no package carries a key; sign-in accounts and memberships are not exported; no other implementation reads or writes such a package; and the hosted reference index gives its complete export only to holders of its token, so a lineage longer than its bounded package is carried there as that package with the older states declared absent.

requirements.summary: Registry relations supersedes, revokes, suspends, expires and disputes are independent of token spending; historical authority precedence applies only within one comparable named trust framework, otherwise the conflict is returned unresolved; antecedents resolve by expected identifier and verified content under bounded traversal.

requirements.notes: Relations supersedes, revokes, suspends and expires (derived at evaluation time) are recorded and served with their source and reason; disputes has no producing path and is listed as not produced; conflicts under different frameworks or anchors are returned unresolved with every candidate named; independent assessments do not compete. From 9 November 2026 the reference registry no longer produces the sources vsc-correction, vsc-parent and status-publication, because it accepts no new SEAL and publishes no status lists; relations recorded under them stay served, which its tests exercise. revokes and suspends now have one producing path, an authenticated status observation made while reporting on a stored record (status-observation); the relation store tests persist and clear relations of that source, and test/external-credentials.test.ts drives an observation through the report into a relation: a set bit on an authenticated revocation or suspension list records revokes or suspends, served on the report and the proof, a forged or stale list records nothing, and an authenticated read of the bit unset marks a suspension cleared and never clears a revocation. Re-read 2026-11-12 after the reference registry removed its legacy intake with the conflict cascade and the certification registry: it no longer produces the source conflict-cascade, so supersedes joins disputes as not produced, and the relations recorded under it stay served. It holds no authority evidence to rank issuers by, so every conflict is returned unresolved with every candidate named; the competing-claim fixture shows timestamp-first would pick the later claim and the registry picks none. requirements.summary: Each observation of an event, each conflict decision, each association index entry, each retention entry, each journal entry of unfinished work, the state of each query pull and each page a pull acknowledged carries its own type and version; a decision names every competing observation and changes none; the index is rebuildable from the retained sources and records and never records a class or quantity reference as an individual item; a pull record holds no credential and its checkpoint is moved only with the record of the page that named it. A store also keeps the record of each recovery snapshot restored into it and of where each original of that snapshot was placed, with the reference it was exported under and the one the restored records carry; an unfinished restore is a journal entry that only the restore can finish; and a pull record lists each declaration that its source is reached at another address.

Every pull record and page record the module writes validates against the schema, the states that exist only between two durable steps included, and the schema refuses a pull record with a member it does not name. The pull tests validate a pull record, a page read ahead of its checkpoint and page records that carry them. The recovery tests validate a restore record, every relocation record, the journal entry of a restore that was stopped and a pull record that carries a declaration, and hold the schema to refusing a restore entry without its snapshot and a relocation record of another version. From that day a recovery snapshot carries the observation, decision, pull and page records as they are stored, apart from cursor material when cursors are excluded (EPCIS-11-operational-recovery); the index entries, the retention entries, the journal and the two records of a restore are not carried. requirements.summary: An authorised recovery snapshot carries, for each source scope it covers, every retained original in its exact bytes and the import records, observations, conflict decisions, pull records and page records that no source can rebuild, and leaves out the associations index, the retention entries and the journal. It is taken at a boundary with no unfinished work, never holds a checkpoint without the imports and pages it stands on or a decision without every observation it decided between, and is described by a descriptor in the evidence envelope. No credential enters it or the public form, cursors are left out unless asked for, and the public form carries no operational record and cannot be restored. A restore checks the descriptor, every file, every record and the invariants before it writes and refuses each failure by its own name; it preserves every identity, receipt time, provenance, decision and query bound, relocates only bytesRef through a checked one-to-one mapping that the destination records, never overwrites a destination record that differs and never merges two source scopes. Afterwards a retry of an acknowledged request answers the same import with no new receipt, the same request identifier with other bytes conflicts, and an interrupted pull continues or replays from its retained bounds without skipping a page or beginning a new source.

requirements.notes: Added 2026-11-15 with the rule. The public tests build one deployment with two source scopes that share an event identifier, a decided conflict with both of its observations, and a pull of four pages that stopped after its second page was retained and before its checkpoint moved. They export it from each shipped storage adapter and restore it into the other, and compare the originals byte for byte, every carried record, and the rebuilt associations index and retention entries with the source's. The restore is stopped before and after every durable call and run again to the same store. They exercise each refusal by name on a snapshot whose digests, inventory and identity were all made to agree again, so that only what the records say can refuse it: a checkpoint without its import or its page, a decision without an observation, a missing and an altered original and record, a descriptor that does not match the inventory, an unknown record version, a misfiled record, a record of one source scope made to stand on a record of another, and records that carry cursor material the descriptor says was left out. They exercise the collisions a restore reports and never overwrites, a retry of an acknowledged request, the same request identifier with other bytes, and a pull resumed with its cursor left out, carried, expired, and at an origin the destination does not permit, and with its source declared at another endpoint. They search every exported byte of both forms for a planted credential in four encodings, the page tokens the source issued and a secret the source wrote into its next-page addresses. The shared adapter suite takes a snapshot of a store, restores it into a second store of the same adapter and stops that restore at every durable call. The boundary is established on the six-method storage interface by the store's turn, by two readings held to equal revisions and by the invariant check, and it assumes one process writes to the store: a writer that changes a record and puts its revision back is not detected. An export refuses while work is journalled and finishes none of it. A snapshot is held in memory while it is assembled and while it is restored. Re-read 2026-11-15 with the application starter, which now carries the snapshot in its complete export and restores it with its restore command. Its exit exercise, packages/create-dpp-app/template/apps/api/test/exit-exercise.test.ts, exports from the starter's MongoDB adapter with three source scopes, two of which share an event identifier, one decided conflict and a pull interrupted after two of four pages, stops that deployment's database and index, and restores into the module's file-system adapter through the signed manifest's inventory: every original is returned byte for byte, every import record, observation, decision and page record equals the exported one apart from bytesRef and the excluded page tokens, the rebuilt associations equal the ones the first deployment held, a repeated request answers the same import with no new receipt, the same request identifier with other bytes conflicts, the source refuses the pull until its credential is configured again, and the pull then replays from its retained bounds with no cursor and no event held twice. Packages assembled without the import a checkpoint stands on, without an observation a decision names, and with one bit of an original changed are refused by name with nothing written. deploy/evidence/exit-exercise.json records a run. Both deployments ran in one test process, so no exit between two independently operated deployments has been exercised, and no claim is made that a snapshot written by one implementation restores into another. Re-read 2026-11-16 after section 1 said that the reference implementation reads a bare event in its parser only, its import and its pull taking whole documents, that an import record keeps at most 1,000 findings, and that the ceilings on a raised limit bound a pull and not a file import; section 8 is unchanged. The exit exercise now writes its package with npm run export and restores it a second time with npm run restore, each run as a process of its own, and restores it into a deployment without the keys, which reads both passports and refuses an UPDATE by name.

requirements.summary: The descriptor of an EPCIS exchange snapshot, format 1, names every file the snapshot needs with its kind, length and SHA-256; the source scopes covered, with what each holds and what became of the cursor of each pull; the boundary the snapshot was taken at; everything left out, with the reason; and what is claimed: complete for the covered scopes and recoverable for an authorised recovery snapshot, or bounded and not recoverable for the public form. Its limits are fixed: no credential is carried, derived indexes are rebuilt at the destination, records are restored as recorded and no origin is established. Its identity is the digest of the inventory it names. It defines no member for a credential, a cursor or a signature of its own.

requirements.notes: Added 2026-11-15 with the contract. A hand-written check, epcisRecoveryProblems, is held to the schema's verdict on 7 accepted and 50 refused descriptors and names the member each problem is at. The rules a schema cannot state are epcisRecoveryInconsistencies: a file or a scope listed twice, a file outside the folder of its kind, an identity that is not the digest of the inventory, counts the inventory does not bear out, a cursor state its mode cannot have and a claim its access path cannot make. A restore refuses a descriptor with any of them, and then holds the records to what the descriptor says of each scope, each pull and the cursors. Every descriptor the module exports in the tests, in both forms and from both shipped storage adapters, validates against the schema. The package does not run the schema at run time.
